title: India's borders: Pakistan and China
summary: Kashmir, the Line of Control and the Line of Actual Control, and why two borders shape India's foreign policy.

stops.caption: India shares long, contested borders with two nuclear-armed neighbours: Pakistan to the west and China to the north.

stops.caption_title: Kashmir and the Line of Control
stops.caption: Since 1947 India and Pakistan have both claimed Kashmir. The Line of Control divides the parts each country holds.
The two countries fought wars in 1947, 1965, 1971 and 1999, and militant attacks have repeatedly set off crises.
With China the border is an undefined Line of Actual Control. Troops clashed in Ladakh's Galwan Valley in 2020.
China claims most of the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, which it calls South Tibet.
Two contested borders push India to build up its military and to deepen partnerships such as the QUAD.
